title: Frozen Registry Lifecycle Reconciliation
problem: Frozen-baseline forward-ports can leave historical exact-head thaw pairs stale, and freshly written authoritative registry state can race CI propagation, causing otherwise-correct proof chains to fail or loop.
root_cause: The frozen V4 registry verifier is intentionally strict and immutable, but API2 had no lifecycle planner to atomically advance shared baselines while retiring obsolete thaw pairs and no bounded state-progress rule for authoritative ref refresh.
patch: Keep the frozen registry verifier untouched. Add a pure lifecycle planner that advances every frozen owner of an explicitly changed baseline in one state transition, retires thaw file-pairs for the moved baseline without rebasing authority, preserves unrelated grants, recomputes revision/hash, and validates the result. Add a pre-verifier authoritative lifecycle audit plus a bounded three-attempt registry ref refresh that stops immediately when the state hash does not advance.

prior_observed_failures: obsolete Step-4 thaw pair after frozen Step-3 baseline forward-port

repair.evidence: The frozen V4 registry rejected keep.py blob values built from k/m because Git blob SHAs must match [0-9a-f]{40}; five Step-6 tests failed before lifecycle behavior was exercised.
repair.patch: Replace only the synthetic keep.py baseline/target values with hex-valid c/d 40-character values and keep all lifecycle semantics unchanged.
